questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly the courses offered by the university, and the I have heard good things about living in Edinburgh.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think in general that there was a lot of information, and we got many emails during that time, which were a little overwhelming at times. However, the university provided a step-by-step guide of what to do upon arrival, which made it easier. So overall I would say fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An introduction meeting and guidance through emails and the web-page. I was also in contact with the student association's advice place, relating to an issue with my accomodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of student accomodation.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a kitchen, which was equipped with all the basic facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you have any issues with your housing, or you are not satisfied with it you should contact the accomodation service, to check if there are other options available. I got my accomodation one week after I arrived by contacting them, because I needed to move out of the flat I was initially staying at. They were very helpful and I got a cheap room in very nice location.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to registrer online and do an international check-in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails, guides and student advisors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One class I really wanted was cancelled, but I ended up getting some very interesting courses, which were high my priority list.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of help available, reach out if you need it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general I thought the level was good, challenging - but not too hard to follow. I took some honours courses which were jointly thought (both for MA and BA). I thought the level were alright, and the expectations were different for BA and MA students. Sometimes I did feel a little bit of a disadvantage in not having a good understanding of the British and Scotish legal system, but the teachers were very understanding of that.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching and the contents of the courses was very different from what I am used to at UCPH. In the courses I took, I thought that critical thinking was much more encourage than it is at UCPH, and I really enjoyed that. I also found that the lectures and seminars was much less case based. I did not have any exams, I was assesed through course work, so I had to write a lot of essays, which we don't do much as UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Law and Power in the Muslim World, The Rule of Law, Global Legal Systems.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Law and Power in the Muslim World; It provided a very critical perspective of the role of international law in maintaining and facilitating the current political order and its embedded hierachies. The readings were very interesting, and it provided an outlook on law that I had not encountered at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Except for housing, I thought that the living cost in Edinburgh were in general fairly cheap compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are loads of societies, hosting all different types of events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I reccomend that you look into the different societies, (I believe there is something for everyone), and then don't be shy about joining their events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking! Scotland is beautiful. Pentland hills is just 40 minutes by bus outside of the city, and there are loads of lovely and accesible hiking paths. The highlands are also worth a few visits, but it can be a little difficult to get there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - most people are extremely kind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of my friends were also internationals. But I would say talking to your course mates, joining a society, and then through student accomodation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. The traffic is interesting - remember to look to your right when crossing the road!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and the pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded and inviting, don't be afraid to ask for help, take the opportunities you are handed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I have met!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
